body:
emily: heads-up: found an Azure SAS token in one of our public CI build logs archived in gs://build-logs/2026/04/12/. It's plain in the stdout of a 3rd-party step.

rajan: SAS token? which storage account? can you paste a redacted snippet?

emily: redacted: 
```
UPLOAD: blob upload to https://redwood-partner.blob.core.windows.net/builds/container.tar?sv=2020-08-04&ss=b&srt=sco&sp=rw&se=2026-04-13T12:34:56Z&st=2026-04-12T12:00:00Z&spr=https&sig=REDACTED
```

tori: That query string looks like a full SAS. If someone leaked that, anyone with the URL could read/write until expiry. Is that our account or partner's?

emily: It's partner-owned container (redwood-partner). The log also shows an env var name AZURE_SAS_TOKEN and a local filename /workspace/.env.staging.

vault-bot: Incident auto-detected: potential credential exposure (azure-sas). Recommended severity: P3.

security-bot: Created INCIDENT-2026-1788 (azure-sas-exposure). Assigning eng-security and infra-oncall.

rajan: Immediate ask: 1) get list of all logs/artifacts with SAS in querystring across our archive. 2) ask partner to revoke the token and rotate their storage keys. 3) check whether we ever used that SAS to pull blobs into our infra.

emily: running a quick grep across gs bucket for "blob.core.windows.net" and "sv=" now. Will post hits in ~10m.

tori: Also check container image layers for embedded .env files. Old build pipeline used to bake env into images. run 'skopeo inspect' or 'dive' on suspect images.

emily: grep found 4 hits in the last 14 days: two build logs, one container layer tarball, one integration-run artifact. Saved to /tmp/sas-hits-1779998889.txt and shared with eng-security drive.

rajan: Partner oncall pinged. They say this SAS was minted by their CI using a legacy service principal that has broad Storage Blob permissions. They will rotate and revoke by EOD if we give affected keys.

emily: shared the /tmp list and timestamps with partner-oncall via secure channel.

ops: quick note: check our outbound logs for any fetches using that URL; we might have mirrored the blob. I'll run a proxy log scan.

ops: scan shows one internal fetch from 2026-04-12 12:05:22 by build-worker-3. It pulled container.tar and unpacked to /tmp.

rajan: If we pulled it, there is a risk of plaintext creds inside. Steps I'd recommend: A1) Partner revokes SAS and rotates storage keys (partner-oncall) A2) Our infra team re-scans container.tar contents and any extracted files for secrets (emily+ops) A3) Rotate any Vault paths that map to AZURE_* envs (tori) A4) Remove legacy service principal from partner RBAC and require managed identity (rajan+partner-oncall) A5) Add CI rule to block querystrings with sv= and signatures showing up in logs (tori)

tori: For Vault rotation, mapping: AZURE_SAS_TOKEN was referenced in secret/path/thirdparty/az/sas. I'll increment version and mark old version as revoked.

emily: scanning container.tar with trivy and custom regexes for azure url patterns and common access key prefixes. Found a file .env.staging with AZURE_SAS_TOKEN present. Extracting and quarantining.

ops: quarantined artifact to gs://internal-quarantine/1779998889/container.tar and added a retention lock until incident closed.

partner-oncall: we revoked the SAS and rotated keys. Confirmed deletion of the specific blob and logs on our side, but asking for a list of timestamps/objects that referenced it so we can scrub their history too.

rajan: shared the timestamps from emily's grep and the container sha. Can partner confirm whether their audit logs show any unrecognized unwrapping or usage?

partner-oncall: audit shows only the CI service principal used it; no external IPs. They will remove tf-legacy-sp and reissue with least-priv role.

security-bot: Note: update audit retention flags for the rotated secrets and log the rotation event to the compliance ledger.

rajan: tori, once you rotate the Vault secret, add a short TTL and change consumer apps to use an Azure Managed Identity or ephemeral SAS minted via our partner's short-lived API.

tori: rotating now: vault kv put secret/path/thirdparty/az/sas value=REDACTED metadata=rotated-by:tori; setting TTL 15m on new tokens and adding note in secret metadata.

emily: CI patch: adding a log-scrubber step that will redact querystrings with sv= and block builds that attempt to echo full URL. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/3210

ops: also dropping an automated alert: if a build worker attempts to write an .env.* file into artifacts, fail the job.

rajan: RBAC: scheduling a short maintenance window with partner to remove legacy SP and replace with managed identity + conditional access. PR sent to partner-admins.

security-bot: Incident update: partner revoked SAS, our Vault secret rotated, artifact quarantined, RBAC PR open. Target: confirm no external exfil and close incident in 24h after review.

emily: ack. I'll run a full repo & artifact history scan overnight and post results here.

tori: ack. I'll also add the CI rule and update onboarding docs to disallow copying env files to partner steps.

partner-oncall: thanks — we'll confirm when their full audit scrub completes.

security-bot: THREAD CLOSED: details moved to INCIDENT-2026-1788 channel for follow-ups.
